summary: Reproduced all 5 unresolved bugs (3,4,5,6, partially 7) directly against the LIVE Railway production API (https://updatedistylistbeauty-marketplace-production.up.railway.app/api) using real Supabase-authenticated customer/provider sessions. CRITICAL DISCOVERY: Railway's deployed backend is a DIFFERENT codebase than /app/backend/server.py in this repo - confirmed via GET /api root: Railway returns {'message':'Beauty Stylist Marketplace API','version':'1.0.0',...} while local server.py's root returns {'message':'Hello World'}. Also, error strings seen from Railway (e.g. 'Could not access conversations', 'Could not access chats') do not exist anywhere in local server.py. This means BUGS 3, 4, 5, 6 (and the already-attempted fix for BUG 2) are rooted in a Railway codebase that is NOT present in this repo and cannot be fixed by editing /app/backend/server.py or the frontend alone - main agent needs to locate/access the actual Railway source repo to fix these. Regression-checked BUG1/8 (feed author name) - passes, real provider data returned by GET /feed/posts.

critical.issue: BUG3 REPRODUCED: Returns HTTP 500 'Failed to create booking: {\'message\': \'column users.moderation_status does not exist\', \'code\': \'42703\'}'. This is a genuine Postgres schema error in Railway's live booking-creation code (references a users.moderation_status column that doesn't exist in the DB). Reproduced with a valid provider_id=13, service_id=8, valid date/time, customer with wallet balance 4900 (service price 4000, so balance IS sufficient). This is NOT a frontend contract bug - the request payload was accepted (no 422), it fails deep inside server-side booking creation logic. Not present in /app/backend/server.py (that file only proxies /bookings to Railway for a wallet pre-check, then forwards - the actual failing SQL is inside Railway's own handler, not in this repo).

BUG4 REPRODUCED: Returns HTTP 502 {'detail':'Could not access conversations'} when a customer tries to start an inquiry with a valid provider_auth_id (the exact call chatService.createInquiry makes from both 'Ask a Question' and 'Ask About Product' buttons). This explains why both buttons appear to 'do nothing' - the fetch does fire, but Alert.alert('Could not start inquiry', ...) should show; if it silently doesn't, that's a secondary UI issue (contacting state loading spinner may mask it briefly) but the ROOT CAUSE is this 502. NOTE: /app/backend/server.py DOES have a matching /conversations/inquiry handler using Supabase directly, and it does NOT reference this 'Could not access conversations' string at all - meaning Railway's live deployment is running different/stale code from what's in this repo.

BUG5 REPRODUCED: Returns HTTP 401 {'detail':'Comment author auth_id is required'} even though the request body correctly includes author_auth_id (matching the exact payload FeedCommentsModal/feed.service.ts sends) AND a valid Bearer token is attached. Tried variants: body only, body+query param, body+auth_id alias - all return the same 401. This endpoint does not exist anywhere in /app/backend/server.py (feed/* is Railway-only per problem statement), so it cannot be fixed by editing this repo.

BUG6 REPRODUCED (real server-side validation, not a frontend bug): a 6024-char base64 image string in the `message` field returns HTTP 422 {'detail':[{'type':'string_too_long','loc':['body','message'],'msg':'String should have at most 4000 characters'}]}. Confirmed this is a genuine Pydantic max_length=4000 constraint on Railway's live schema for the `message` field - any real photo's base64 will exceed this. The frontend/backend contract needs to either upload images to storage and send a URL, or raise the server-side limit (not fixable from local repo since this endpoint's Pydantic model is on Railway).

While regression-checking the already-applied BUG2 fix (message_type='location'), Railway's live endpoint returned HTTP 400 {'detail':'Unsupported message type'} for message_type='location'/'LOCATION'/'Location'. Even message_type='text' on this same conversation now returns HTTP 502 {'detail':'Could not access chats'}. This means the entire /conversations/{id}/messages endpoint appears broken/unstable on the live Railway deployment right now, regardless of message_type - so the BUG2 fix (sendLocationMessage) cannot be verified as actually working against production; it may still show a failure to the user. This is independent of the frontend fix's correctness - it's a live-backend-side failure.

minor.issue: BUG7: response contains NO avatar/photo/image field at all (checked keys containing 'photo'/'avatar'/'image' - none present) for provider id=13. Could not fully verify cache-busting/URL-reuse behavior since the endpoint doesn't return an avatar URL in the first place for this test provider; recommend retesting with a provider that has actually uploaded a photo.

integration_issues.flow: Ask a Question / Ask About Product (BUG4)
integration_issues.issue: chatService.createInquiry hits POST /conversations/inquiry which returns 502 on the live API. The catch block does call Alert.alert('Could not start inquiry', err.friendlyMessage) so the user should see SOME alert, not total silence - but since the review request says 'nothing visible happens', worth double-checking on-device whether Alert.alert is actually rendering (not a code issue found in shop/[id].tsx or provider/[id].tsx logic itself; both correctly guard on stylist_auth_id/user_id and both are populated in the real API responses we fetched).

action_items: HIGH PRIORITY: Determine where Railway's ACTUAL deployed source code lives - confirmed it is NOT identical to /app/backend/server.py (different root endpoint response, different/missing error strings). Editing this repo's backend/server.py will NOT fix bugs 3,4,5,6 in production since Railway isn't running this code for those endpoints.
BUG3: Report the Postgres error 'column users.moderation_status does not exist' to whoever owns the Railway/Supabase schema - likely a missing migration on the `users` table.
BUG4: Investigate why Railway's live /conversations/inquiry returns 502 'Could not access conversations' - this exact error string is not in this repo, confirming stale/different deployed code.
BUG5: Investigate why Railway's live /feed/posts/{id}/comments rejects a correctly-populated author_auth_id body field with 401.

BUG6: Either raise the message field's max_length on Railway's Pydantic model for chat messages, or (better) change the image-sharing flow to upload the photo to storage and send a URL instead of inline base64 - current 4000-char cap makes any real photo impossible to send.

BUG2 regression risk: Confirm with main agent/product owner whether the already-shipped location-sharing fix can even work today, since Railway's /conversations/{id}/messages is currently rejecting 'location' message_type (400) and even 'text' (502) on this tested conversation.
BUG7: Retest avatar propagation using a provider that has an actual photo_url/avatarUrl set (test provider used had none in full-profile response).
critical_code_review_comments: chat.service.ts sendLocationMessage/sendMessage assume Railway accepts message_type='location' - not currently true per live test; frontend code itself is not at fault here.
provider.service.ts normalizeProvider correctly maps 'provider_id' -> id and would work fine IF the /bookings creation on Railway didn't 500 first.

rca_of_issue: BUG3: 500 Postgres 'column users.moderation_status does not exist' inside Railway's live POST /bookings handler - DB migration/schema issue, not a payload issue (payload accepted, wallet balance sufficient). BUG4: 502 'Could not access conversations' from Railway's live POST /conversations/inquiry - generic error message not found in local repo, implies an unhandled exception in Railway's actual (different) implementation of this route. BUG5: 401 'Comment author auth_id is required' from Railway's live POST /feed/posts/{id}/comments despite author_auth_id being present in the body and matching what feed.service.ts sends - endpoint not in local repo at all. BUG6: genuine 422 Pydantic max_length=4000 validation on the `message` field for chat messages - base64-encoded photos always exceed this, so the reported 'Could not send photo' error text the user sees is real and server-enforced, not a client mistake.
